Unitree G1 EDU+ · Open Day greeter

What the stand will look like

The real G1 model from Unitree, standing still, with the Brio webcam on our printed chest bracket. Press play to watch one visit: a visitor in green walks up, the robot notices them, invites them over, chats on the talk spot and says goodbye. The small window shows what the webcam itself sees.

How it works

Chest webcamBrio, 640×480, 30 fps
→
Person trackingYOLO pose + BoT-SORT with ReID, on the Jetson
→
Scenegreen clothing, distance, facing, groups, crowd
→
Interaction ladderidle → noticed → bid → open → converse → close
→
Voice modelOpenAI Realtime, sees a webcam frame each turn; fallbacks
Head depth cameraD435i, 47.6° down
→
Talk spotsomeone standing 0.6–1.4 m ahead
→
Built-in mic and speakerrobot's 4-mic array in, chest speaker out

Everything runs in one process on the robot's own computer (Jetson Orin NX). The robot never moves: no arm, waist or walking commands exist in the code. No face recognition; it only talks about clothing and objects.

Where things stand

Done

  • Greeter software written; 148 automated tests pass on a laptop, with the robot, camera and cloud replaced by stand-ins
  • Webcam (Brio 4K) and 1 m cable bought
  • Chest bracket designed, checked against Unitree's 3D model, test-printed
  • Code and guides on GitHub, with a public guide site

Next, on the robot

  • Record the built-in mic in wake-up mode; decide whether an extra mic is needed
  • Set up the Jetson, deploy, run the self-test
  • Full visit with a lab webcam, then fit the Brio on the bracket
  • Decide: invite anyone, or only people in green

Not yet known

  • Real latency and audio quality in a noisy hall
  • Whether the depth camera is free to use alongside Unitree's own services
  • How visitors respond (the paper plan covers the study)
